topic: Volume: cylinder minus sphere from reference-sheet formulas
problem: A closed cylindrical container has an interior radius of 6 centimeters and an interior height of 15 centimeters. A solid sphere with a radius of 3 centimeters is placed inside the container, and the rest of the container is completely filled with water. What is the volume, in cubic centimeters, of the water in the container?

bad.why: Nothing unknown needs solving: the volume is a direct computation from the givens, so graphing adds steps without removing any math.

algebraFirst.description: Computes 6^2(15) = 540 and (4/3)(3^3) = 36 by hand, then subtracts: 540pi - 36pi = 504pi.

explanationNotes: The water fills all the space the sphere does not take up, so its volume is the cylinder's volume pi r^2 h minus the sphere's volume (4/3)pi r^3, both printed on the SAT reference sheet. Dividing the result by pi shows 504, which matches the choice written as a multiple of pi; 540pi is the trap of forgetting to subtract the sphere.
